story_facts_verified.property: 171-177 and 185-191 South High Street, Columbus (also 200 South Wall Street), Franklin County Auditor parcel 010-008456-00. Three vacant, fire-damaged brick storefronts in the Downtown District, across High Street from Columbus Commons and next to the former Ohio National Bank building (167 S. High St., parcel 010-037820-00), which the owner has separately renovated.
story_facts_verified.owner: Town High Plaza, LLC, which took title February 13, 2023 (Limited Warranty Deed, Instrument No. 202302210016351). Independent coverage (Hoodline, ABC6/FOX28) describes the owner as an LLC affiliated with Cleveland-based Harsax Management.
story_facts_verified.commission_decision: Downtown Commission case COA2600161. The owner applied February 25, 2026 and, rather than a replacement building, offered a plan to maintain the cleared lot as a seeded lawn. At the March 24, 2026 meeting the commission voted 3-3; under its rules the tie is deemed a denial. The three negative votes cited the absence of a proposed replacement structure or use (Joint Stipulation of Facts, para. 12-15).
story_facts_verified.code_basis: Columbus City Code 3359.23 bars a downtown demolition permit without a certificate of appropriateness, which may issue only if (1) a replacement use is approved, or (2) if no replacement is proposed, a maintenance plan is approved. The property is not on the Columbus Register of Historic Properties, so the Historic Resources Commission has no role (Stipulation para. 10-11).
story_facts_verified.enforcement_history: May 14, 2019 Unsafe Building Order UNSF1900122 (fire damage); 2022 code-enforcement suit (Franklin County Municipal Court 2022EVH060251), voluntarily dismissed December 29, 2022 to facilitate a sale to a buyer committed to demolition; April 10, 2023 reissued Unsafe Building Orders; August 29, 2025 code-enforcement suit (2025EVH060528) in which the City itself seeks receivership and demolition (Stipulation para. 3-9).
story_facts_verified.appeal_status: Administrative Appeal AA0001-2026 of COA2600161, filed April 2, 2026 under CCC 3359.05(E). Columbus Legistar shows MatterStatusName 'Second Reading', MatterBodyName 'Zoning Committee', MatterIntroDate 2026-10-02, MatterAgendaDate 2026-10-05; public notice PN0377-2026 sets oral arguments for Monday, October 5, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. No Council action/vote has occurred yet (histories empty as of this run).
story_facts_verified.positions: Appellant argues CCC 3359.23(2) allows a certificate with a maintenance plan and no replacement, and that the Commission nullified that option by requiring a building (appellant reply brief). The City, as appellee, argues the application proposed only a vacant lot with a grass lawn and that the Downtown Design Guidelines adopted in Ordinance 1532-2013 counsel against vacant lots and non-accessory parking, and asks Council to affirm (City appellee brief). Columbus Landmarks placed the block on its 2023 Most Endangered list and urged reuse (Hoodline).
story_facts_verified.original_contributions: Direct reading of the Legistar appeal record and the appeal's joint Stipulation of Facts and both parties' briefs (pulled and text-extracted this run); a timeline reconciling the Commission's stipulated March 24, 2026 meeting date and 3-3 vote against press framing of an 'April' denial; the identification of the parallel 2025 City receivership suit seeking the same demolition the Commission blocked; and a CREN locator map of the block.
story_facts_verified.limitations_stated: Council has not ruled; the article reports a scheduled hearing, not an outcome, and makes no prediction. The owner-Harsax affiliation is reported by news outlets, not the stipulated record (which names Town High Plaza, LLC). The parallel receivership suit remains pending. Exact building square footage (~38,300 sq ft) comes from news coverage, not the stipulation, and is not asserted as a verified figure in the article.
